name: imbalance_auc
description: Known-item retrieval over a corpus on imbalanced tabular classification and AUC optimisation. Every question is deliberately paraphrased away from its gold paper's title wording, so a lexical channel cannot win by copying the title back. Read `rationale` before changing any gold: a gold that is merely on-topic is not a gold.

queries.question: Train on convex combinations of two examples, mixing both the inputs and their labels with a coefficient drawn from a Beta distribution.
queries.rationale: mixup. The paper's own title says nothing about beta distributions or interpolation, so a title-copying channel gets no help here.

queries.question: Define the uncertainty set as a transport-distance ball centred on the empirical distribution and optimise against the worst case inside it.
queries.rationale: Wasserstein DRO. Explicitly NOT `arxiv:2203.00176` (When AUC meets DRO): that one uses KL divergence and CVaR and never mentions Wasserstein — an early version of this set had it as gold, which is exactly the mislabel the usability check exists to catch.

queries.question: Ask whether the two standard capacity-control tricks are still needed once batch normalisation is in the network.
queries.rationale: Do deep nets really need weight decay and dropout. The question names neither of the two tricks, so the channel has to bridge 'capacity control' to them.

queries.question: Optimise only the area under a restricted stretch of the ROC curve, bounded to a false-positive-rate interval, instead of the whole curve.
queries.rationale: Two-Way Partial AUC and the partial-AUC SVM paper. This is the query where lexical ranking collapses: 67 chunks match across 17 papers and a clinical paper that uses 'specificity' as a metric name floods the top of the list.

queries.question: A broad review of how deep models behave when one class vastly outnumbers the other, and what has been tried about it.
queries.rationale: Survey on deep learning with class imbalance. Kept deliberately: `majority`/`minority` are the topic words here, so any IDF scheme that down-weights common terms must not break this one.

queries.question: Optimise a ranking objective in a single sweep over the data without keeping earlier examples around.
queries.rationale: One-Pass AUC Optimization. 'Ranking objective' rather than AUC, so the channel must bridge the synonym.

queries.question: Optimise a ranking objective when only positive examples are labelled and everything else is unlabelled.
queries.rationale: Semi-Supervised AUC Optimization based on Positive-Unlabeled Learning.

queries.question: Swap the objective of a gradient-boosted tree ensemble for one that up-weights hard examples, to cope with skewed labels.
queries.rationale: Imbalance-XGBoost and Robust-GBDT. Two papers are genuinely correct here; the rank of whichever comes first is what counts.

queries.question: Use a generative model to turn examples of the abundant class into examples of the rare class for tabular data.
queries.rationale: Imbalanced Classification via a Tabular Translation GAN.

queries.question: Generate new rare-class rows by sampling inside the convex hull spanned by the rare-class neighbourhood.
queries.rationale: ConvGeN. 'Convex hull' is the paraphrase of the paper's 'convex space'.

queries.question: Several parties hold their own data and optimise a ranking objective jointly without the number of communication rounds growing with the iterations.
queries.rationale: The two federated AUC maximisation papers.

queries.question: Systematically compare the available remedies for skewed class frequencies on convolutional architectures.
queries.rationale: A systematic study of the class imbalance problem in convolutional neural networks.
